question: Why do some asteroids hit Earth before any telescope has seen them coming?
answer: Asteroids can hit Earth before any telescope has seen them because the Sun's side of the sky is a blind spot. A ground telescope's circle of view does not cover that part of the sky. Switching to infrared changes what you can see, which the page invites you to compare.
move: The Sun’s side of the sky is our blind spot.

web.label: A sky view with Earth at the centre and a rock you can drag around it. A circle marks what a ground telescope can see. A switch changes the view to infrared. The question asks why some asteroids hit before telescopes spot them.
